Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

secondly adverb

also second, in the second place, firstly … secondly, first of all … then, thirdly

classical

Cic. Att. 6.3.1: prīmum quod vidētur esse honōs … deinde quod sōlum habeō praetōrium
Ter. Heaut. 3: Id prīmum dīcam: deinde quod vēnī ēloquar.

deinde

adverb; after prīmum

secondly, next (in a list of points)

Latin counts its points prīmum … deinde … tum … postrēmō (or dēnique), and may repeat deinde for a third point. Its plain sense is “then, next” in time (see then).

Other words

  • secundō — secondly, in the second place

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Planc. 50 (Lewis & Short): prīmum, ut honōre dignus essem, maximē semper labōrāvī; secundō, ut existimārer; tertium …

    Lewis & Short calls it rare: Cicero once, Phaedrus with prīmō. Later it is also “for the second time”.

  • alterum (est) — the second point (of two)

    neuter of alter, as a noun · also used · classical

    Where there are only two points, alter is “the second”: ūnum … alterum …, the one … the other (see another).

Examples

  • prīmum est dēvium, deinde ab Autrōniō et cēterīs quadriduī, deinde sine tē.

    Firstly, it’s off the road; secondly, it’s four days from Autronius and the rest; and thirdly, it’s without you.Cic. Att. 3.7.1

  • Id prīmum dīcam: deinde quod vēnī ēloquar.

    I’ll explain that first; then I’ll say what I’ve come for.Ter. Heaut. 3

See also then, finally, another, begin, second.
